label: Diagram 11.2
caption: Diagram 11.2 Relevant boundary
description: A schematic diagram, titled at the bottom "Diagram 11.2 Relevant boundary", with "See para 11.5" at top left. At the centre is a solid square labelled "Building", with labels inside it for its sides: A (left), B1 (right), B2 (bottom) and C (top). Dashed lines around it represent boundaries. A vertical dashed line on the left coincides with side A; a vertical dashed line on the right is parallel to B1; a horizontal dashed line below is parallel to B2. From the top-left corner a diagonal dashed line runs up and right, forming an angle marked "< 80°" with a horizontal dashed extension. Leader lines join each boundary to text: "This boundary coincides with and is therefore relevant to side A"; "This boundary is parallel to and therefore relevant to side B1"; "The boundary is parallel to side B2"; "This boundary is at less than 80 degrees to side C and is therefore relevant to side C"; and "But the relevant boundary may be the centre line of a road, railway, canal or river", pointing to a dashed line at the bottom. A NOTES panel on the right states the diagram sets out the rules for a boundary to be considered relevant, and lists rules a, b and c, restating that a relevant boundary coincides with side A, is parallel to B1 or B2, or is at a maximum of 80 degrees to side C.
